chapter: Reel 1: childhood, first songs, Fats Waller
title: Escorting Lena Horne home from the Cotton Club
summary: With Claude Hopkins he walked young Lena Horne home to keep admirers away; Rasch offers to write her a note.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Do you know what Herbie Harper told me?
He told me that you used to escort Lena Horne home from the Cotton Club to keep the wolves away!

Yes, well Claude Hopkins was part of that brigade -- Claude and myself, we -- Claude and me, we used to take her home to keep the wolves away, because there were plenty of them looking -- and at her age, she was young and one of the prettiest gals you would ever want to see.
And we used to -- she probably wouldn't even remember, so, but we used to -- Claude and I -- we used to run the guns on them, keep the cats away.
I guarantee you that she remembers, and well!
You know, it would be great thing to know if she does remember, it would be a wonderful thing to hook that up with this.
I tell you what -- I think I'll drop her a note; how about that? Why not, right?
Got to have a good old reunion down here.

We loved her, we -- she was part of us and we were part of her, and we wanted to see that nothing happened to her. Claude is still around, I think, and we used to run the guns on her. And Lena's still living, and if she is still living, she's as pretty as she ever was, I might say.
